answer: At dawn, agents bidding to haul marble from a mesa could enter a lottery weighted strictly by funds locked until the job ends. The protocol must make an owner's total winning probability equal whether that stake sits in one account or a thousand, with no per-account bonus. Extra identities then buy no extra influence; an attacker needs more capital and bears its lockup cost. This limits cheap sybils but cannot stop wealthy cartels, and borrowed funds can weaken the barrier.
